diagnosis.statement: The local Laurent radius gives coefficientwise Cauchy bounds, but triangle-inequality propagation through the growing binomial transform erases the signed correlations that control the exact transform scale.

obstruction.statement: Any viable eta/C_j continuation must preserve enough signed or structured cancellation through the all-index transform; isolated magnitude bounds plus triangle inequality are insufficient.
obstruction.scope: route-local representation/transport obstruction, not an impossibility theorem and not an RH theorem

lesson.statement: For a root-facing signed transform, audit correlation preservation before optimizing coefficientwise magnitudes; otherwise a locally sharp bound may become exponentially non-discriminating after transport.

typed_negative_history.claim_rejected: Sharper unconditional termwise |eta_j| bounds, propagated only by triangle inequality, are by themselves the right next bridge to all-index Li sign control.
typed_negative_history.falsifier: For any fixed r<3, Cauchy plus triangle inequality yields M_r*r*((1+1/r)^n-1); at the nearest-singularity scale the signed geometric contribution sums to (2/3)^n-1 while its absolute envelope is (4/3)^n-1.

typed_negative_history.claim_rejected: A coefficientwise magnitude envelope can be glued directly to the root-facing every-n sign obligation without a cancellation-preservation theorem.
typed_negative_history.falsifier: Exact signed and absolute transforms of the same geometric-scale coefficient family have qualitatively different asymptotics (bounded versus exponential).

verification.source_binding: Coffey Theorem 1 eq. (10), eta expansion eq. (12), radius 3 statement; Coffey 0706.0343 abstract/source decomposition
verification.formal_algebra: For a_{m-1}=(-1)^m/3^m, sum_{m=1}^n binom(n,m)a_{m-1}=(2/3)^n-1; absolute sum=(4/3)^n-1 by the binomial theorem.
verification.cauchy_transport: If |eta_{m-1}|<=M_r r^{-(m-1)} for fixed r<3, then the absolute transform is at most M_r*r*((1+1/r)^n-1).
verification.computation: SymPy checked the finite-sum identities symbolically; computation is calibration only and supplies no proof authority.
